projects.title: Detecting Fraudulent Health Insurance Claims
projects.blurb: A machine learning study analyzing 20,100 health insurance claims
projects.content:
**Business Objective:**
- The project aims to build a machine learning triage tool that ranks 20,100 historical health insurance claims by fraud risk
- This ensures investigators focus their manual reviews on the most suspicious claims, balancing the high cost of a missed fraud against the time cost of a false alarm

**Methodology:**
- The data analysis included a crucial safeguard: splitting the data into training and test sets before duplicating the fraud rows for class balancing
- This prevented data leakage and ensured the models were evaluated on genuinely unseen claims
- Six supervised algorithms and one unsupervised algorithm (K-Means) were compared

**Key Findings:**
- XGBoost emerged as the best-performing model, achieving an ROC-AUC score of 0.874
- The strongest drivers of fraud were identified as Specialist Office providers (which had a nearly 50% fraud rate), high procedure counts, elevated cost per procedure, and longer distances between the patient and provider

**Recommendations & Next Steps:**
- The exact probability cut-off for flagging a claim should be determined by comparing the insurer's investigation costs against average fraudulent payouts
- Since the current dataset uses synthetic data, the next critical step is to validate the model's performance on a real claims extract

projects.title: Customer insights dashboard
projects.blurb: One shared view of customer behaviour, replacing four teams' conflicting reports.
projects.content:
## The problem

Four teams each maintained their own definition of an active customer. Meetings started with an argument about whose number was right.

## What I did

- Ran a short workshop to agree on one definition, in writing
- Modelled the metric once in dbt so every report reads from the same source
- Built a single dashboard and deprecated the other reports deliberately, with notice

## Result

The definitional argument stopped. Adoption was helped more by turning the old reports off than by building the new one.

projects.title: Supply chain optimisation
projects.blurb: A routing and inventory model that found meaningful annual savings.
projects.content:
## The problem

Stock was allocated to warehouses using a rule written years earlier that nobody had revisited.

## What I did

- Framed allocation as a linear programme with real capacity and lead-time constraints
- Validated against a year of historical data before proposing any change
- Presented the result as a range, not a single number, so operations could weigh the risk

## Result

The recommended reallocation was adopted for two regions and produced measurable savings in the first two quarters.
